questions.q: In superdense coding, how many qubits does Alice physically transmit to Bob, and how many classical bits does she send?
options: She physically transmits 1 qubit and sends 2 classical bits of information
She physically transmits 2 qubits and sends 2 classical bits
She physically transmits 1 qubit and sends 1 classical bit
She physically transmits 0 qubits and sends 4 classical bits
questions.explain: Only Alice's half of the pre-shared Bell pair is physically sent -- Bob's half never moves -- yet Bob can recover 2 full classical bits, double the usual 1-bit-per-qubit limit.

questions.q: To encode the message '11', what gate sequence does Alice apply to her own qubit, and what does the Bell pair (0.7071, 0, 0, 0.7071) become?
options: X then Z, producing (0, 0.7071, -0.7071, 0)
Z then X, producing (0.7071, 0, 0, -0.7071)
Only H, producing (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
I, leaving the state unchanged
questions.explain: Verified directly: applying X to q1 swaps the |00> and |11> amplitudes to |01> and |10>, then Z flips the sign of whichever term now has q1=1, giving (0, 0.7071, -0.7071, 0).

questions.q: What two gates does Bob apply, in what order, to decode the message after receiving Alice's qubit?
options: CNOT(q1→q2), then H on q1, then measure both qubits
H on q1, then CNOT(q2→q1)
Only a measurement, no gates needed
Z on q2, then X on q1
questions.explain: Bob's decode step mirrors the Bell-pair preparation in reverse: CNOT with q1 as control and q2 as target, followed by H on q1, then measurement of both qubits reads out exactly the 2 bits Alice encoded.

questions.q: Why doesn't superdense coding's 2-bits-per-qubit result violate any classical channel-capacity limit?
options: The Bell pair had to be created and physically distributed in advance, which itself cost one qubit transmission -- that earlier 'hidden cost' is what makes the later doubling possible
It does violate the limit, but only in laboratory conditions
Classical channel-capacity limits don't apply to entangled particles at all
Because Bob secretly already knew the message before Alice sent anything
questions.explain: The full accounting includes the earlier qubit transmission needed to distribute the entangled pair -- once that's counted, no capacity law is broken; the protocol just front-loads cost into the setup phase.

questions.q: Which single-qubit gate encodes the message '00' in the superdense coding protocol?
options: I (identity -- no gate applied)
X
Z
X then Z
questions.explain: Applying no gate at all (I) leaves the Bell pair exactly as it started, (0.7071, 0, 0, 0.7071), which Bob's decode procedure reads out as '00'.
